blueprint_concepts: Vectors applied to prove trigonometric and geometric results
english: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $BC=4$, $CA=5$ and $AB=6$. As $P$ varies over all points in space, the minimum value of $PA^{2}+PB^{2}+2PC^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $ABC$ एक त्रिभुज है जिसमें $BC=4$, $CA=5$ तथा $AB=6$ है। जब $P$ अन्तरिक्ष के सभी बिन्दुओं पर परिवर्तित होता है, तब $PA^{2}+PB^{2}+2PC^{2}$ का न्यूनतम मान ______ है।
solution: Take the origin at the point $G$ with $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}+2\overrightarrow{c}=\overrightarrow{0}$ (position vectors of $A,B,C$), $P$ at $\overrightarrow{p}$
solution_full: Choose the origin at the point $G$ whose position vector is $\dfrac{\overrightarrow{A}+\overrightarrow{B}+2\overrightarrow{C}}{4}$; then the position vectors $\overrightarrow{a},\overrightarrow{b},\overrightarrow{c}$ of $A,B,C$ satisfy $\overrightarrow{a}+\overrightarrow{b}+2\overrightarrow{c}=\overrightarrow{0}$. Let $P$ have position vector $\overrightarrow{p}$.

Hence $S\ge K$ with equality only for $\overrightarrow{p}=\overrightarrow{0}$, i.e. $P=G$ (a point of the plane $ABC$). The minimum is $K=|\overrightarrow{a}|^2+|\overrightarrow{b}|^2+2|\overrightarrow{c}|^2$.
To express $K$ by the sides, expand: $AB^2=|\overrightarrow{a}-\overrightarrow{b}|^2$, $BC^2=|\overrightarrow{b}-\overrightarrow{c}|^2$, $CA^2=|\overrightarrow{c}-\overrightarrow{a}|^2$, so
Adding the two lines, the dot products cancel: $AB^2+2BC^2+2CA^2=4|\overrightarrow{a}|^2+4|\overrightarrow{b}|^2+8|\overrightarrow{c}|^2=4K$.
originality_note: New: a weighted sum of squared distances with weights 1, 1, 2 is minimised by moving the origin to the weighted centroid; the minimum is then turned into side lengths by the vector identity |a + b + 2c|^2 = 0 (way 4). Closest known: PA^2 + PB^2 + PC^2 = 3PG^2 + GA^2 + GB^2 + GC^2 (Leibniz) with equal weights. Different because: unequal weights move the minimising point off the centroid and change the side-length formula to (c^2 + 2a^2 + 2b^2)/4.

concept_use.Vectors applied to prove trigonometric a: Vector proof of the geometric result S = 4 PG^2 + K and of K = (AB^2 + 2BC^2 + 2CA^2)/4 through |a + b + 2c|^2 = 0.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked numerically with coordinates for the 4-5-6 triangle (minimum 29.5 at (A + B + 2C)/4). Changed: No change.
key_step: Shifting the origin to (A + B + 2C)/4 so the linear term vanishes, then writing the constant through side lengths.
justification: A known vector technique (Leibniz-type identity) applied with unequal weights; several routine expansions, no deep idea. Like 2021-P2-Q18 (L2), a vector-geometry extremum with a standard core.
